cards.text: God has a message for Israel, and it comes through a man named Malachi. The Bible calls it “the burden of the word of the LORD,” so you know this one's got WEIGHT. It's like when your phone lights up with a text that just says “Got a minute?”

cards.question: Here come the LORD's first words to Israel through Malachi. What does He tell them?
Israel hears the LORD say “I have loved you” and takes it right in, no questions asked.

cards.text: Nope. Israel fires right back: “How have You loved us?” That's like telling somebody “I love you” and they look up and go, “Okay. Show your work.”
So the LORD answers with a question of His own: “Was not Esau Jacob’s brother?” Esau and Jacob were twin sons of Isaac (Genesis 25:24-26), and later God renamed Jacob as Israel (Genesis 32:28).

cards.question: The LORD is talking to Israel, the people who came from Jacob. Which brother does He say He has loved?

cards.text: Jacob. Then the LORD says, “but Esau I have hated,” and He points to what's become of Esau's land.

cards.question: The LORD says He has made Esau's mountains a ___.
The LORD says He left Esau's inheritance to the desert jackals.

cards.text: Edom, Esau's people (Genesis 36:1), may say, “We have been devastated, but we will rebuild the ruins.” I respect that, because when MY edges got wrecked, I rolled into a junk drawer and stayed there for YEARS.

cards.question: Edom plans to rebuild the ruins. What does the LORD of Hosts say about that?

answers.text: He will tear down what they build
He will help them build it back
He will let them build in peace

cards.question: The LORD says He will be indignant with Edom for only a little while.

cards.text: Forever. Edom will be called the Land of Wickedness, and then the LORD turns back to Israel: “You will see this with your own eyes.”

cards.question: Israel will see all this for themselves. What does the LORD say they will end up saying about Him?

answers.text: He is great even beyond Israel
He is great only inside Israel
He has stepped away from Israel

cards.text: That's it. They'll say, “The LORD is great—even beyond the borders of Israel.” From “Show your work” to THAT, friend? Now that's a turnaround.

findings.problem: Stop 1, card 10 quotes "We have been devastated, but we will rebuild the ruins.", which isn't the exact BSB wording.

rule.text: Quotes: Quotation marks around Bible words mean the exact BSB wording, punctuation included.

findings.problem: Stop 1, card 13 quotes "You will see this with your own eyes.", which isn't the exact BSB wording.

rule.text: Quotes: Quotation marks around Bible words mean the exact BSB wording, punctuation included.

findings.problem: Nothing before card 2 sets up a message of love. Card 1 actually points the other way. It calls the message a burden with WEIGHT and compares it to an ominous "Got a minute?" text, which nudges a thoughtful baker toward "I have judged you." The only way to get it right is to ignore the setup.

rule.text: Before each choice card, Papa Dorin's story card gives enough context that the baker can reason their way to the answer.

findings.problem: The joke "Okay. Show your work." is a schoolroom phrase, from a teacher grading homework. It makes school the comparison for Israel's question.

rule.text: No jokes or scenarios about school, parents or anything aimed at kids.

findings.problem: The card says "God renamed Jacob as Israel (Genesis 32:28)." In Genesis 32:24-28 the text calls the one who renames Jacob "a man." The cited verse doesn't state what the card says. Genesis 35:10, where God renames Jacob, would support the line as written.

rule.text: Call things what the text calls them.

findings.problem: Two answers are single names ("Jacob" and "Esau"). The third, "Both brothers the same," is a different kind of answer and much longer, so it stands out.

rule.text: All the answers are the same kind of thing, about the same length and the same tone.

findings.problem: Card 9 asks whether the next words of verse 3 are "left Esau's inheritance to the desert jackals." That tests exact wording the baker hasn't seen. Nothing on earlier cards lets the baker reason out the jackals detail, so this is luck, not reasoning. It also comes right after card 8 asked about the first half of the same line.

rule.text: Never ask the baker to guess the next words of a line.

findings.problem: Papa Dorin says "I rolled into a junk drawer and stayed there for YEARS," which makes it sound like he went in on his own. In his backstory, Mother Miller picked him up and slid him into the junk drawer. The line changes his backstory.

rule.text: His backstory, family, bakery and mission are the Dorinverse story in this file. He can talk about them freely, but never adds anything new to them.

findings.problem: The callback "From 'Show your work' to THAT" repeats the school-phrase joke from card 4.

rule.text: No jokes or scenarios about school, parents or anything aimed at kids.

findings.problem: "Now that's a turnaround" presents Israel's question in 1:2 and their future words in 1:5 as a change of heart. The text only says what they will see and say. It doesn't connect the two as a turnaround.

rule.text: Leave open what the text leaves open: who is being spoken to, why, or how two things connect.
